title: Atomic TF apply orchestrator and GPU lease fencer for private installs
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduce an atomic orchestrator that slices Terraform applies into transactional stages, adds a GPU lease-fencing mechanism to prevent double-allocation during rolling upgrades, and provides a staged rollback hook for private deployments.
description: Context: Private deployments rely on a large set of interdependent Terraform modules (VPC, subnet claims, GPU nodepools, IAM bindings). Existing bulk applies make incremental upgrades risky: partial applies can leave GPU leases allocated while nodepools are in transition, and network changes can cause irreversible drift. Motivation: provide a deterministic, operator-driven apply flow that can be staged, validated, and atomically rolled back without manual state surgery. What this PR does: 1) Adds an 'apply-orchestrator' binary and terraform helper module that breaks a full apply into ordered slices (network -> IAM -> subnet-claims -> gpu-nodepools -> post-rollout hooks). Each slice is applied with a snapshot of the backend state and an optional pre-check plan; failures stop the pipeline and trigger a rollback boundary. 2) Introduces a 'gpu_lease_fencer' Terraform module + controller hook: when a tenant requests GPU capacity, the fencer creates an immutable lease object and an apply-lock tag on nodepool resources; the orchestrator will honor leases during scaling and drain/replace operations to avoid double allocation. 3) Implements 'staged rollback hooks' that capture the last known-good state snapshot, run curated undo plans for the most dangerous modules (nodepool and subnet claim), and ensure IAM bindings are reconciled after rollback. 4) Adds health checks and a circuit-breaker for long-running GPU pool updates: if an apply slice exceeds a configured time budget or error rate, orchestrator aborts and surfaces remediation steps. 5) Documentation and examples showing a safe canary/rollout for tenant-scoped GPU pool upgrades. Migration notes: the orchestrator is opt-in; existing users continue to use the legacy terraform workflow. Operators can enable orchestrator by adding a small wrapper config in their pipeline: a) register a backend snapshot bucket, b) enable lease-fencer module in tenant module, c) add orchestrator configmap for slice ordering and timeouts. Testing: unit tests for orchestrator state machine, integration tests that run against a local terraform backend (minio) to validate atomic apply and rollback semantics, manual dry-run on staging with two tenants and simulated AZ failures. Rollout plan: enable behind a feature flag in Private-installer 0.46; run canary on non-prod clusters for two weeks; open support channel for early adopters. Related: ENG-1128 (safe-gpu-upgrades), SRE-204 (tfstate incidents). Checklist: [x] design doc updated [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] docs + example pipeline [x] rollout plan and runbook.
